name: Eastmark Center of Industry Phase II — 52.89 acres
address: SEC Everton Terrace & Mesquite Road, Mesa, AZ 85212
parcelStatus: Exact offered parcels and legal description not reconciled
availability: Public broker marketing observed 2026-10-29; seller availability and control terms not confirmed
claims: JLL ID 743589 offers 52.89 acres for sale or build-to-suit, with price on request.
Broker identifies Planned Community zoning and proximity to the Elliot Road Technology Corridor. This is not verified data-center permission.
No allocated MW, substation capacity, service date or fiber routes are established for the offered parcel.

buyerMatches.why: Specific corridor fit: NTT PH1 is on the Elliot Road Technology Corridor at 10256 Elliot Road, with a 102-acre/240 MW campus plan and 36 MW critical-IT first building. The offered 52.89-acre land provides a plausible smaller phased-campus hypothesis in the same technology district, rather than a generic Arizona match. It is not established as adjoining NTT or needed beyond its controlled pipeline.
buyerMatches.specificTest: Ask NTT whether additional Mesa land has an active customer mandate. Test net usable layout for an initial building, on-site substation and three truly diverse fiber entrances, mirroring PH1 project evidence rather than treating those specifications as universal acquisition requirements.

blockingQuestions: Does the Planned Community entitlement allow the proposed data-center use, generators, height and cooling plant?
What is the exact offered boundary, APN schedule and net buildable area?
Can three independent fiber entry routes be secured and can the substation/utility corridor fit?
Would NTT prefer to use remaining controlled Mesa land instead of acquiring this site?
capitalFit: Price and option terms unverified; assume buyer-backed acquisition or seller partnership, not a low-cost speculative option.
forecastStatus: No calibrated site-specific construction probability; any numerical forecast must be explicitly labeled a conditional planning scenario and exclude unverified buyer interest.
nextAction: Obtain current seller availability, APNs, offered boundary, control economics and actual utility documents before paid diligence.

Brochure claims Industrial/Tech Campus zoning, a south-boundary fiber easement and an easement to a 200 MW substation. These are marketing statements; the substation rating is not available site load.
Brochure includes 2023 market data and future power-system plans; current utility allocation and the land remaining unsold require revalidation.

buyerMatches.why: Aligned operates a 55-acre West Jordan campus and SLC-04 in West Valley City and explicitly markets Utah cooling economics, carrier access and closed-loop air/liquid cooling. This 100-acre divisible, technology-zoned offering is a concrete regional campus alternative with room to test modular expansion and external plant. Eagle Mountain is not adjacent to either Aligned campus; regional overlap alone does not establish suitability.
buyerMatches.specificTest: Verify that Aligned has a customer whose service region accepts Eagle Mountain; measure diverse fiber routes back to its required Utah nodes, obtain a current load-service offer, and test closed-loop cooling/module geometry with water use and electrical infrastructure on net usable land.

name: Cermak Square — marketed urban data-center development
askingPriceText: Broker marketing indicates approximately $40 million land value and $140 million proposed-project listing; obtain current separate land/shell scope and firm asking terms.
parcelStatus: Exact offered parcels and legal description not reconciled
availability: Broker marketing re-published May 2026 and JLL syndicated listing is indexed as available; direct LoopNet fetch restricted and Showcase redirected. Treat as research lead pending written availability and seller control verification.
sourceType: Broker offering on JLL-syndicated marketplace plus dated Castles Unlimited broker article
claims: JLL broker Sean Reynolds markets a proposed multi-story data-center development for lease/purchase; Castles Unlimited published a dated May 8, 2026 offering article.
Broker describes an approved Planned Development and approximately 363,000 square feet across seven floors; approval documents were not reviewed.
Broker cites 40 MW eventual capacity with 16 MW at completion and additional 8 MW increments. These are unverified future power claims, with MW basis unspecified.
Offering is described as two blocks from 350 East Cermak. This is a location claim, not proof of a diverse fiber extension or campus cross-connect eligibility.
Public delivery claims conflict: 15 versus 19 months and August 2027. They require a new construction and utility schedule.
Land acreage is deliberately withheld: listing databases appear to mix building square footage and land area; legal boundary and survey are required.

buyerMatches.why: More specific than a metro match: Equinix CH1, CH2 and CH4 operate at 350 E Cermak, and the offered development is marketed two blocks away. This could be an IBX infill or powered-shell arrangement tied to the existing interconnection ecosystem, subject to fiber engineering and customer demand. It is not an xScale rural-campus match.
buyerMatches.specificTest: Obtain two or more physically independent fiber paths into the existing Cermak ecosystem, Equinix engineering acceptance of campus-extension distances, usable floor-load and liquid-cooling design, and a current ComEd delivery schedule. Determine whether Equinix would acquire land, lease a shell, or reject the offered developer economics.

buyerMatches.why: CoreSite CH2 demonstrates a purpose-built multi-story downtown Chicago model with 18 MW, high-density support, three diverse fiber entries and connectivity to its Chicago ecosystem. Cermak Square offers the same urban development type near the major Cermak carrier hub; it is not adjacent to CH2 and has no demonstrated CoreSite interest.
buyerMatches.specificTest: Price a diverse dark-fiber extension to CH1/CH2 and establish customer latency and connectivity economics. Compare the offered seven-floor plan, floor loading and equipment yards with CoreSite design requirements, and test whether expansion of its controlled Chicago facilities is superior.

blockingQuestions: Is bare land separately purchasable today, and who controls the permitted development?
What are the exact acreage, APNs, legal description, title and existing use?
Can the actual Planned Development approval and permitted data-center floor plan be supplied?
What current utility agreement supports each phase, and is its MW facility load or IT critical load?
Are the 2027 delivery statements still valid and is the proposed seven-floor design compatible with current AI cooling and floor loads?
Can developer economics support an operator-owned build or shell lease at the disclosed land/project pricing?
capitalFit: Institutional buyer-backed development; approximately $40 million land indication is unsuitable for speculative self-funded acquisition. Seller JV or buyer-backed option would require negotiation.
forecastStatus: No calibrated site-specific construction probability; any numerical forecast must be explicitly labeled a conditional planning scenario and exclude unverified buyer interest.
nextAction: Obtain current seller availability, APNs, offered boundary, control economics and actual utility documents before paid diligence.

buyerMatches.why: A concrete Hillsboro ownership expansion hypothesis: Flexential acquired its Hillsboro 6 land in September 2025 for a 350,000-square-foot, two-story, 27 MW facility and states a preference for facility ownership. This marketed 32.07-acre campus land sale fits that ownership and purpose-built model more closely than a small generic Portland lot. It is not established as adjacent to its existing campuses.
buyerMatches.specificTest: Compare current Hillsboro 6 absorption and customer commitments against need for another parcel. Test carrier-route integration into FlexAnywhere, a multi-story high-density layout, utility deliverability and an actual land-sale boundary before assuming the industrial plan can become a data center.

buyerMatches.why: Switch already markets its Tahoe Reno campus around dedicated fiber to the Bay Area and Las Vegas. A data-center-approved 75-acre TRIC parcel is therefore a coherent extension-area screen, contingent on whether Switch wants additional land beyond its owned campus. Same industrial park does not establish shared boundaries, network access or power rights.
buyerMatches.specificTest: First reconfirm sale availability. Then establish whether Switch has incremental land demand and whether the specific boundary supports its required closed-loop EVO design, future phases and permitted dark-fiber route into its existing network. Do not infer that nearby utility infrastructure is accessible to Switch.

blockingQuestions: Is this still for sale and what exact APNs and development approvals convey?
Is there incremental buyer need beyond Switch-owned Tahoe Reno land?
Can the parcel connect to Switch network routes without a single shared choke point?
Will the EVO closed-loop architecture fit within net usable area and cooling/noise limits?
